records.source: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֨ר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י הָל֞וֹךְ וְקָנִ֤יתָ לְּךָ֙ אֵז֣וֹר פִּשְׁתִּ֔ים וְשַׂמְתּ֖וֹ עַל־מָתְנֶ֑יךָ וּבַמַּ֖יִם לֹ֥א תְבִאֵֽהוּ׃
records.gloss: Thus said Yahweh to me: go and buy for yourself a loincloth of linen and put it on your loins, and into water not bring it.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said this to me: "Go and buy a linen loincloth and put it on around your waist, but do not put it in water."

L.1: Thus said {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} to me: "Go and buy yourself a linen loincloth and put it on your waist, but do not let it come into water."

R.1: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me: "Go and buy a linen loincloth, a cloth that wraps around the waist. Put it on, but do not get it wet."

decisions.choice: loincloth: a linen cloth wrapped around the hips and waist, worn next to the skin
decisions.reason: The word names something tied around the waist (Isaiah 11:5; 2 Kings 1:8, where Elijah's is of leather). It was worn close against the body, and that closeness is the point of the picture in verse 11. Linen was fine cloth; the priests' garments were made of it (Leviticus 16:4).

decisions.choice: do not put it in water: keep it as it is, unwashed
decisions.reason: The text does not say why. The command probably keeps the cloth new and untouched by water until it is hidden, so that its ruin later comes only from the place where it lay (verse 7).

decisions.choice: a sign acted out: the prophet's actions carry the message
decisions.reason: Prophets sometimes acted out what God was saying (Isaiah 20:2-4; Ezekiel 4-5; Jeremiah 19; 27). The meaning of this action is given in verses 9-11.

decisions.choice: loincloth; Readable adds what it is
decisions.reason: "Belt" or "sash" would suggest something worn over clothing, but the garment was wrapped around the body itself. Readable explains the word once.

records.heading: The ruined loincloth

records.source: וָאֶקְנֶ֥ה אֶת־הָאֵז֖וֹר כִּדְבַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה וָאָשִׂ֖ם עַל־מָתְנָֽי׃ס
records.gloss: And I bought the loincloth according to [the] word of Yahweh, and I put [it] on my loins.
pieces: So I bought the loincloth as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me and put it on around my waist.

L.2: So I bought the loincloth according to the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and put [it] on my waist.

R.2: So I bought the loincloth, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had told me, and I put it on.

decisions.choice: according to the word of the LORD: Jeremiah does exactly what he is told
decisions.reason: The story repeats each command and then says it was carried out (verses 5 and 7). The prophet's obedience stands against the people, who "refuse to listen" (verse 10).

records.source: וַיְהִ֧י דְבַר־יְהוָ֛ה אֵלַ֖י שֵׁנִ֥ית לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me a second [time], saying:
pieces: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me a second time:

L.3: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me a second time, saying:

R.3: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me a second message:

decisions.choice: a second time: a new message after the first command was carried out
decisions.reason: Each step of the sign begins with a fresh word from God (verses 1, 3, 6, 8).

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me, saying (Literal); came to me (Balanced); gave me a message (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's usual wording for this formula at each level.

records.source: קַ֧ח אֶת־הָאֵז֛וֹר אֲשֶׁ֥ר קָנִ֖יתָ אֲשֶׁ֣ר עַל־מָתְנֶ֑יךָ וְקוּם֙ לֵ֣ךְ פְּרָ֔תָה וְטָמְנֵ֥הוּ שָׁ֖ם בִּנְקִ֥יק הַסָּֽלַע׃
records.gloss: Take the loincloth which you bought, which [is] on your loins, and arise, go to Perath and hide it there in [a] cleft of the rock.
pieces: "Take the loincloth you bought, the one you are wearing, and set out for the Euphrates. Hide it there in a crack in the rock."

L.4: "Take the loincloth that you bought, which [is] on your waist, and arise, go to Perath and hide it there in a cleft of the rock."

R.4: "Take the loincloth you bought and are wearing. Go to the Euphrates River and hide it there in a crack in the rocks."

decisions.choice: Perath: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: Perath is the Hebrew name of the Euphrates everywhere else (Genesis 2:14; 2 Kings 24:7; Jeremiah 46:2, 6, 10; 51:63), and Babylon, the power that would ruin Judah, lay on that river. But the Euphrates was hundreds of miles from Anathoth, and Jeremiah goes there twice, journeys of months. So the place may instead be Parah, a town of Benjamin (Joshua 18:23) a few miles northeast of Anathoth, in a valley of springs and rock clefts that still has a similar name. Its name would then call up the great river. The text does not settle which is meant.

decisions.choice: arise, go: set out
decisions.reason: "Arise" before another verb of motion means to get going; it does not imply that Jeremiah was sitting or lying down.

decisions.choice: a cleft of the rock: a crack or hollow in a rocky bank
decisions.reason: The same word is used of the clefts in rocks where people hid (16:16; Isaiah 7:19). Hidden in damp ground by water, linen soon rots.

decisions.choice: Perath (Literal); the Euphrates (Balanced); the Euphrates River (Readable)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew name, which leaves open the question in m1; Balanced and Readable give the usual meaning of the name. The footnote gives the other place.

records.source: וָאֵלֵ֕ךְ וָאֶטְמְנֵ֖הוּ בִּפְרָ֑ת כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר צִוָּ֥ה יְהוָ֖ה אוֹתִֽי׃
records.gloss: And I went and hid it at Perath, just as had commanded Yahweh me.
pieces: So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded me.

L.5: So I went and hid it at Perath, as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded me.

R.5: So I went and hid it by the Euphrates, just as {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had commanded me.

decisions.choice: at Perath: beside the river, or at the place so named
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

decisions.choice: Perath (Literal); the Euphrates (Balanced and Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4.

records.source: וַיְהִ֕י מִקֵּ֖ץ יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וַיֹּ֨אמֶר יְהוָ֜ה אֵלַ֗י ק֚וּם לֵ֣ךְ פְּרָ֔תָה וְקַ֤ח מִשָּׁם֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֵז֔וֹר אֲשֶׁ֥ר צִוִּיתִ֖יךָ לְטָמְנוֹ־שָֽׁם׃
records.gloss: And it was at [the] end of many days, and said Yahweh to me: arise, go to Perath and take from there the loincloth which I commanded you to hide there.
pieces: After many days {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Set out for the Euphrates and take from there the loincloth I commanded you to hide there."

L.6: And it came about at the end of many days that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Arise, go to Perath and take from there the loincloth that I commanded you to hide there."

R.6: A long time later, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to me, "Go to the Euphrates River. Get the loincloth that I told you to hide there."

decisions.choice: at the end of many days: after a long time, its length not given
decisions.reason: Long enough for the linen to rot in the damp hiding place.

decisions.choice: set out (Balanced); go (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 4, "arise, go" means to set out.

records.source: וָאֵלֵ֣ךְ פְּרָ֔תָה וָאֶחְפֹּ֗ר וָֽאֶקַּח֙ אֶת־הָ֣אֵז֔וֹר מִן־הַמָּק֖וֹם אֲשֶׁר־טְמַנְתִּ֣יו שָׁ֑מָּה וְהִנֵּה֙ נִשְׁחַ֣ת הָאֵז֔וֹר לֹ֥א יִצְלַ֖ח לַכֹּֽל׃פ
records.gloss: And I went to Perath and I dug and I took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it there; and look, ruined [was] the loincloth; not it was fit for anything.
pieces: So I went to the Euphrates and dug, and I took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it. And there it was, ruined, of no use for anything.

L.7: So I went to Perath and dug, and took the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it; and look, the loincloth was ruined; it was not fit for anything.

R.7: So I went to the Euphrates. I dug up the loincloth from the place where I had hidden it. But it was rotten and could not be used for anything.

decisions.choice: ruined: spoiled, rotted
decisions.reason: The same verb returns in verse 9, where God says "I will ruin" the pride of Judah. The ruined cloth is the picture; verse 9 gives what it means.

decisions.choice: not fit for anything: completely useless
decisions.reason: The verb means to succeed or be fit for a use. The same words close verse 10, tying the cloth to the people.

decisions.choice: look (Literal); there it was (Balanced)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word draws attention to what was found. Modern English has no single word for it; Readable shows it by "But".

records.source: וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר־יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And came [the] word of Yahweh to me, saying:
pieces: Then the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me:

L.8: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to me, saying:

R.8: Then {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave me this message:

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came: God now explains the sign
decisions.reason: After the action comes its meaning (verses 9-11).

decisions.choice: the word of the LORD came to me, saying
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

records.source: כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֑ה כָּ֠כָה אַשְׁחִ֞ית אֶת־גְּא֧וֹן יְהוּדָ֛ה וְאֶת־גְּא֥וֹן יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם הָרָֽב׃
records.gloss: Thus says Yahweh: thus I will ruin [the] pride of Judah and [the] pride of Jerusalem the great.
pieces: "{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: This is how I will ruin Judah's pride, the great pride of Jerusalem.

L.9: "Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: In this way I will ruin the pride of Judah and the great pride of Jerusalem.

R.9: "This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I will ruin Judah's pride and the great pride of Jerusalem in the same way.

decisions.choice: pride: both the splendor Judah boasted of and its arrogance
decisions.reason: The word can mean majesty (Nahum 2:3, "the pride of Jacob") and also arrogance (48:29). Here it covers both: the city, temple and kingdom Judah was proud of, and the proud spirit that would not listen (verses 15, 17).

decisions.choice: in this way: as the loincloth was ruined
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used of the loincloth in verse 7.

decisions.choice: great: describes the pride
decisions.reason: The word "great" agrees in form with "pride", not with Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: Thus says the LORD (Literal); The LORD says this (Balanced); This is what the LORD says (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's usual wording for the formula. God's speech runs to the end of verse 14 and is quoted in double quotation marks in this prose account.

records.source: הָעָם֩ הַזֶּ֨ה הָרָ֜ע הַֽמֵּאֲנִ֣ים׀לִשְׁמ֣וֹעַ אֶת־דְּבָרַ֗י הַהֹֽלְכִים֙ בִּשְׁרִר֣וּת לִבָּ֔ם וַיֵּלְכ֗וּ אַֽחֲרֵי֙ אֱלֹהִ֣ים אֲחֵרִ֔ים לְעָבְדָ֖ם וּלְהִשְׁתַּחֲוֺ֣ת לָהֶ֑ם וִיהִי֙ כָּאֵז֣וֹר הַזֶּ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר לֹא־יִצְלַ֖ח לַכֹּֽל׃
records.gloss: The people the this, the evil, the refusing to hear my words, the walking in [the] stubbornness of their heart, and they have walked after gods other to serve them and to bow down to them, and let it be like the loincloth the this which not is fit for anything.
pieces: This evil people, who refuse to hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, who follow the stubbornness of their hearts and have gone after other gods to serve and worship them, will be like this loincloth, of no use for anything.

L.10: This evil people, who refuse to hear {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words, who walk in the stubbornness of their heart and have gone after other gods to serve them and to bow down to them, let it be like this loincloth, which is not fit for anything.

R.10: These people are evil. They refuse to listen to {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} words. They stubbornly follow their own hearts. They have gone after other gods to serve them and worship them. So they will become like this loincloth, which cannot be used for anything.

decisions.choice: let it be: what must come about
decisions.reason: The verb is a wish or command form ("let it be"). Spoken by God, it says what will certainly happen to the people.

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of their heart: following their own will against God's
decisions.reason: The phrase is used for Israel's refusal to listen (Deuteronomy 29:18; Jeremiah 3:17; 7:24). The heart is the seat of will and thought.

decisions.choice: gone after other gods: given them the loyalty owed to the LORD
decisions.reason: To "go after" someone is to follow and serve him; the covenant forbids going after other gods (Deuteronomy 6:14; 8:19).

decisions.choice: the stubbornness of their hearts (Balanced); stubbornly follow their own hearts (Readable)
alternatives: the stubbornness of their evil hearts
decisions.reason: The book's usual wording, without "evil", which this verse does not have with "heart" (compare 7:24, which does).

decisions.choice: worship; will be (Balanced); will become (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Bow down" is the act of worship and is put that way. The wish form "let it be" is given as what will happen (m1).

records.source: כִּ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ יִדְבַּ֨ק הָאֵז֜וֹר אֶל־מָתְנֵי־אִ֗ישׁ כֵּ֣ן הִדְבַּ֣קְתִּי אֵ֠לַי אֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֨ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֜ל וְאֶת־כָּל־בֵּ֤ית יְהוּדָה֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה לִֽהְי֥וֹת לִי֙ לְעָ֔ם וּלְשֵׁ֥ם וְלִתְהִלָּ֖ה וּלְתִפְאָ֑רֶת וְלֹ֖א שָׁמֵֽעוּ׃
records.gloss: For as clings the loincloth to [the] loins of a man, so I made cling to me all [the] house of Israel and all [the] house of Judah, declares Yahweh, to be for me for a people and for a name and for praise and for honor; and not they listened.
pieces: For as a loincloth clings to a man's waist, so I made all the house of Israel and all the house of Judah cling to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people and to bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} renown, praise and honor. But they would not listen.

L.11: For as the loincloth clings to the waist of a man, so I made the whole house of Israel and the whole house of Judah cling to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, to be for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a people, and a name, and praise, and honor; but they did not listen.

R.11: A loincloth clings tightly to a man's waist. In the same way, I made all the people of Israel and all the people of Judah cling to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I wanted them to be {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} people and to bring {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} fame, praise and honor. But they would not listen.

decisions.choice: cling: hold fast in loyal closeness
decisions.reason: The verb is used of Israel holding fast to the LORD (Deuteronomy 10:20; 11:22; 30:20) and of a man clinging to his wife (Genesis 2:24). As the cloth was worn against Jeremiah's body, God bound his people close to himself.

decisions.choice: a people, a name, praise and honor: the covenant purpose
decisions.reason: Deuteronomy 26:19 uses the same three words, praise, name and honor, for what God would make of Israel. Israel was to make God's name known and bring him praise among the nations (compare 33:9).

decisions.choice: the house of Israel and the house of Judah: the whole people, north and south
decisions.reason: Both kingdoms are named; the northern one had already gone into exile a century before, and Judah is now about to follow.

decisions.choice: honor
decisions.reason: This word means beauty or splendor. "Glory" is kept for another Hebrew word (verse 16), so this one is "honor" here.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel; I wanted them
decisions.reason: Readable says "people" for "house" and puts God's purpose as a new sentence.

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֨אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם אֶת־הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֗הסכֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל כָּל־נֵ֖בֶל יִמָּ֣לֵא יָ֑יִן וְאָמְר֣וּ אֵלֶ֔יךָ הֲיָדֹ֨עַ֙ לֹ֣א נֵדַ֔ע כִּ֥י כָל־נֵ֖בֶל יִמָּ֥לֵא יָֽיִן׃
records.gloss: And you will say to them this word: thus says Yahweh [the] God of Israel: every jar will be filled [with] wine. And they will say to you: knowing, do not we know that every jar will be filled [with] wine?
pieces: So say this word to them: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says this: Every jar will be filled with wine.' And they will answer you, 'Do we not know very well that every jar will be filled with wine?'

L.12: And you shall speak this word to them: 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel: Every jar will be filled [with] wine.' And they will say to you, 'Do we not surely know that every jar will be filled [with] wine?'

R.12: Tell them this message: 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of Israel, says: Every jar will be filled with wine.' They will answer you, 'Of course we know that every jar will be filled with wine!'

decisions.choice: jar: a large clay storage jar
decisions.reason: The word can also mean a skin bag, but jars that are smashed against each other (verse 14) are pottery. It is used of a potter's jar in Isaiah 30:14 and Lamentations 4:2.

decisions.choice: every jar will be filled with wine: a saying everyone knows
decisions.reason: The words sound like a common saying, perhaps a drinkers' one. The hearers answer that it is obvious; verse 13 turns it into a picture of judgment.

decisions.choice: do we not surely know: a scornful question
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis. The people mock a message that seems to say nothing new.

decisions.choice: Of course we know
decisions.reason: Readable gives the scornful question as the statement it implies.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks inside God's speech
decisions.reason: God's words to Jeremiah are already quoted (verses 9-14), so the words Jeremiah is to say, and the people's answer, take single marks.

records.source: וְאָמַרְתָּ֨אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם כֹּֽה־אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה הִנְנִ֣י מְמַלֵּ֣א אֶת־כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֣י הָאָ֪רֶץ הַזֹּ֟את וְאֶת־הַמְּלָכִ֣ים הַיֹּשְׁבִים֩ לְדָוִ֨ד עַל־כִּסְא֜וֹ וְאֶת־הַכֹּהֲנִ֣ים וְאֶת־הַנְּבִיאִ֗ים וְאֵ֛ת כָּל־יֹשְׁבֵ֥י יְרוּשָׁלִָ֖ם שִׁכָּרֽוֹן׃
records.gloss: And you will say to them: thus says Yahweh: here I [am] filling all [the] inhabitants of the land the this, and the kings who sit for David on his throne, and the priests and the prophets and all [the] inhabitants of Jerusalem, [with] drunkenness.
pieces: Then say to them, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} says this: I am going to fill everyone who lives in this land with drunkenness: the kings who sit on David's throne, and the priests, the prophets and all who live in Jerusalem.

L.13: Then you shall say to them, 'Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}: Look, I am about to fill all the inhabitants of this land, and the kings who sit for David on his throne, and the priests, and the prophets, and all the inhabitants of Jerusalem [with] drunkenness.

R.13: Then tell them, 'This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} says: I am going to make everyone who lives in this land drunk. That includes the kings who rule from David's throne, the priests, the prophets and everyone who lives in Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: drunkenness: helpless confusion under God's judgment
decisions.reason: The people are the jars, and what fills them is not cheer but a stupor that leaves them unable to stand or act. The same picture is the cup of God's anger (25:15-28; Isaiah 51:17; Psalm 60:5).

decisions.choice: the kings who sit for David on his throne: the kings of David's line, ruling in his place
decisions.reason: "For David" means as his heirs. Every leader is named: kings, priests, prophets and people.

decisions.choice: I am about to fill: the participle points to something soon to happen
decisions.reason: The form after "look, I" describes an action already under way or close at hand.

decisions.choice: with drunkenness / make ... drunk, placed early
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names everyone first and saves "drunkenness" for the last word. Balanced and Readable say it before the list so the sentence stays clear.

records.source: וְנִפַּצְתִּים֩ אִ֨ישׁ אֶל־אָחִ֜יו וְהָאָב֧וֹת וְהַבָּנִ֛ים יַחְדָּ֖ו נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה לֹֽא־אֶחְמ֧וֹל וְלֹֽא־אָח֛וּס וְלֹ֥א אֲרַחֵ֖ם מֵהַשְׁחִיתָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And I will smash them a man against his brother, and the fathers and the sons together, declares Yahweh; not I will pity and not I will spare and not I will have compassion from destroying them.
pieces: I will smash them against one another, {{gender:parents and children|fathers and sons}} alike, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will not pity them or spare them or show them compassion; nothing will keep {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from destroying them.'"

L.14: And I will smash them a man against his brother, the fathers and the sons together, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will not pity, and I will not spare, and I will not have compassion, [so as to keep] from destroying them.'"

R.14: I will smash them against each other like jars, {{gender:parents and children|fathers and sons}} alike, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will not feel sorry for them or spare them or show them mercy. Nothing will stop {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} from destroying them.'"

decisions.choice: smash: shatter, as pottery is shattered
decisions.reason: The verb is used of breaking clay jars and pots (22:28; 48:12; Psalm 2:9). The jars of verse 12 are dashed against each other.

decisions.choice: a man against his brother: against one another
decisions.reason: The phrase is the usual Hebrew way of saying "each other". Fathers and sons together stand for every generation.

decisions.choice: not pity, not spare, not have compassion, from destroying them: nothing will hold back the judgment
decisions.reason: Three verbs of mercy are denied in a row. "From destroying them" says what mercy would have held God back from.

decisions.choice: parents and children (fathers and sons as the alternative)
decisions.reason: "Fathers and sons" here stands for the whole population, young and old, so the inclusive form is the default.

decisions.choice: like jars
decisions.reason: Readable adds the link to the jars of verse 12, which the verb carries in the Hebrew.

records.source: שִׁמְע֥וּ וְהַאֲזִ֖ינוּ אַל־תִּגְבָּ֑הוּ כִּ֥י יְהוָ֖ה דִּבֵּֽר׃
records.gloss: Hear and give ear; do not be haughty, for Yahweh has spoken.
pieces: Listen and pay attention; do not be proud, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.

L.15: Hear and give ear; do not be proud, \q for {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.

R.15: Listen carefully, and do not be proud. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} has spoken.

decisions.choice: hear and give ear: the prophet now calls the people in a poem
decisions.reason: After the prose account of the loincloth and the jars, verses 15-27 are poetry. Jeremiah speaks to the people in verses 15-17, God's own words follow, and the voices are woven together as in other oracles.

decisions.choice: be proud: lift yourselves up, refuse to listen
decisions.reason: The verb means to be high. It answers the "pride" of verse 9: the proud will not bow to God's word (verse 17).

decisions.choice: Listen carefully
decisions.reason: Readable puts the two verbs for hearing into one phrase.

records.heading: Do not be proud

records.source: תְּנוּ֩ לַיהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵיכֶ֤ם כָּבוֹד֙ בְּטֶ֣רֶם יַחְשִׁ֔ךְ וּבְטֶ֛רֶם יִֽתְנַגְּפ֥וּ רַגְלֵיכֶ֖ם עַל־הָ֣רֵי נָ֑שֶׁף וְקִוִּיתֶ֤ם לְאוֹר֙ וְשָׂמָ֣הּ לְצַלְמָ֔וֶת וְשִׁ֖ית לַעֲרָפֶֽל׃
records.gloss: Give to Yahweh your God glory before he brings darkness and before stumble your feet on mountains of twilight; and you will wait for light, and he will make it deep darkness, [and] make [it] thick darkness.
pieces: Give glory to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God before {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes it dark, \q before your feet stumble on the mountains at dusk. \q You will look for light, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will turn it into deep darkness \q and make it black gloom.

L.16: Give glory to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God before {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brings darkness, \q and before your feet stumble on the mountains of twilight, \q and you wait for light, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} makes it deep darkness \q [and] turns [it] into thick gloom.

R.16: Give glory to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} your God before {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} lets darkness fall, \q before you stumble on the mountains as night comes. \q You will hope for light, but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will turn it into deep darkness, \q thick and black.

decisions.choice: give glory to the LORD: honor him by confessing your sin and turning back to him
decisions.reason: The same words are said to Achan when he is called to confess (Joshua 7:19) and to the Philistines when they must admit the God of Israel has struck them (1 Samuel 6:5).

decisions.choice: mountains of twilight: travelers caught on mountain paths as night falls
decisions.reason: On rough hill paths in the dark a traveler loses the way and falls. The picture is of judgment arriving while the people still wait for things to get better.

decisions.choice: makes it thick darkness: the form read aloud
decisions.reason: The written consonants give "he will make"; the scribes marked a slightly different form, "and making", to be read aloud. Both say the same thing.

decisions.choice: deep darkness
decisions.reason: The word is used for the darkest gloom (Job 10:21; Amos 5:8). Its form looks like "shadow" and "death" joined, and it has long been read that way in Psalm 23:4; here it is plain deep darkness, set beside "thick darkness".

decisions.choice: glory
decisions.reason: This is the key term "glory", kept at every level.

records.source: וְאִם֙ לֹ֣א תִשְׁמָע֔וּהָ בְּמִסְתָּרִ֥ים תִּבְכֶּֽה־נַפְשִׁ֖י מִפְּנֵ֣י גֵוָ֑ה וְדָמֹ֨עַ תִּדְמַ֜ע וְתֵרַ֤ד עֵינִי֙ דִּמְעָ֔ה כִּ֥י נִשְׁבָּ֖ה עֵ֥דֶר יְהוָֽה׃ס
records.gloss: And if not you will hear it, in secret places will weep my soul because of pride; and weeping it will weep and will run down my eye [with] tears, because has been taken captive [the] flock of Yahweh.
pieces: But if you will not listen, \q I will weep in hiding over your pride. \q My eyes will weep bitterly and overflow with tears, \q because the flock of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been carried off into captivity.

L.17: But if you will not hear it, \q my soul will weep in secret places because of [your] pride; \q and my eye will weep bitterly and run down with tears, \q because the flock of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has been taken captive.

R.17: But if you do not listen, \q I will cry alone because you are so proud. \q Tears will pour from my eyes, \q because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} flock, the people of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, has been taken away as captives.

decisions.choice: my soul, my eye: the prophet speaks
decisions.reason: The speaker refers to God as "the LORD" and weeps for the LORD's flock, so these are Jeremiah's own words, as in 8:23. He grieves in private over the coming disaster.

decisions.choice: pride: the people's pride
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "because of pride"; the context (verses 9, 15) shows whose it is.

decisions.choice: has been taken captive: what is certain is spoken of as done
decisions.reason: The verb is a past form. It may look ahead to a certain exile as if it had already happened, or speak of the exile of 597 BC, when the king and queen mother of verse 18 were taken (2 Kings 24:12-15).

decisions.choice: the flock of the LORD: his people
decisions.reason: God's people are often pictured as his flock and their rulers as shepherds (23:1-4; Psalm 100:3).

decisions.choice: I will weep (Balanced); I will cry alone, Tears will pour (Readable)
decisions.reason: "My soul" means "I myself". Readable puts the doubled verb for weeping, which stresses how bitter the tears are, as tears pouring down.

records.source: אֱמֹ֥ר לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְלַגְּבִירָ֖ה הַשְׁפִּ֣ילוּ שֵׁ֑בוּ כִּ֤י יָרַד֙ מַרְאֲשׁ֣וֹתֵיכֶ֔ם עֲטֶ֖רֶת תִּֽפְאַרְתְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: Say to the king and to the queen mother: make low, sit, for has come down from your head-places [the] crown of your splendor.
pieces: Say to the king and to the queen mother, "Step down and sit in a lowly place, \q for your splendid crowns have fallen from your heads."

L.18: Say to the king and to the queen mother, "Make yourselves low; sit down, \q for the crown of your splendor has come down from your heads."

R.18: Tell the king and his mother, the queen mother, "Get down from your thrones and sit in a low place. \q Your beautiful crowns have fallen from your heads."

decisions.choice: queen mother: the king's mother, who held an office of honor at court
decisions.reason: The word means "lady" or "mistress". The mother of the reigning king had a throne beside his (1 Kings 2:19) and a rank that could be taken away (1 Kings 15:13; 2 Kings 10:13). The books of Kings name the mother of each king of Judah.

decisions.choice: the king and the queen mother: probably Jehoiachin and his mother Nehushta
decisions.reason: Jehoiachin, who reigned three months, surrendered in 597 BC and was taken to Babylon with his mother (2 Kings 24:8, 12, 15). Jeremiah names the two together in 22:26 and 29:2. The verse names no one, so another king and his mother may be meant.

decisions.choice: make yourselves low, sit down: leave the throne for a place of disgrace
decisions.reason: The two commands together mean to sit low down, as mourners and captives did (48:18; Isaiah 47:1).

decisions.choice: from your heads
decisions.reason: The word means the place at the head (as in Genesis 28:11, where Jacob sets a stone "at his head"). The crowns are knocked from the heads of the king and his mother.

decisions.choice: his mother; get down from your thrones
decisions.reason: Readable says who the queen mother is and what "make yourselves low" meant for a king: coming down from the throne.

decisions.choice: splendid crowns (Balanced); beautiful crowns (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew "crown" is singular, shared by the two; the plural "heads" shows that each wore one. The word for splendor is the one rendered "honor" in verse 11.

records.heading: To the king and the queen mother

records.source: עָרֵ֥י הַנֶּ֛גֶב סֻגְּר֖וּ וְאֵ֣ין פֹּתֵ֑חַ הָגְלָ֧ת יְהוּדָ֛ה כֻּלָּ֖הּ הָגְלָ֥ת שְׁלוֹמִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: [The] cities of the Negev are shut up, and there is no one opening; Judah has been exiled, all of it; it has been exiled completely.
pieces: The towns of the Negev are shut tight, with no one to open them. \q All Judah has been taken into exile, carried away completely.

L.19: The cities of the Negev are shut up, and there is no one to open [them]; \q Judah has been carried into exile, all of it, carried into exile completely.

R.19: The towns in the Negev, in the far south, are shut, and no one can open them. \q All the people of Judah have been taken away as captives, every last one.

decisions.choice: the cities of the Negev shut up: even the far south cut off
decisions.reason: The Negev is the dry land in the south of Judah, farthest from an enemy coming from the north. Its towns are shut, under siege or abandoned, with no one to open the gates. If even they are closed, the whole land is lost.

decisions.choice: has been carried into exile: certain future spoken of as done
decisions.reason: As in verse 17.

decisions.choice: completely
decisions.reason: The word is related to "whole" and "peace" and here means "in full". Amos 1:6, 9 speaks in the same way of a "complete exile" of a whole population.

decisions.choice: in the far south
decisions.reason: Readable says where the Negev was, since the point is its distance from the enemy.

records.source: שְׂא֤וּ עֵֽינֵיכֶם֙ וּרְא֔וּ הַבָּאִ֖ים מִצָּפ֑וֹן אַיֵּ֗ה הָעֵ֨דֶר֙ נִתַּן־לָ֔ךְ צֹ֖אן תִּפְאַרְתֵּֽךְ׃
records.gloss: Lift up your eyes and see those coming from [the] north; where [is] the flock [that] was given to you, [the] sheep of your splendor?
pieces: Look up and see \q the ones coming from the north! \q Where is the flock that was entrusted to you, \q your fine flock of sheep?

L.20: Lift up your eyes and see \q those coming from the north. \q Where [is] the flock that was given to you, \q the sheep of your splendor?

R.20: Look up and see the enemy coming from the north! \q Where are the people who were put in your care, \q your beautiful flock?

decisions.choice: lift up, see: the forms read aloud are plural
decisions.reason: The written consonants have commands to one woman, as the rest of the verse speaks to "you" (a woman). The scribes marked plural forms to be read aloud. Either way it is Jerusalem, and its people, who are told to look.

decisions.choice: those coming from the north: the enemy Jeremiah has spoken of from the beginning
decisions.reason: The disaster from the north is announced in 1:14-15; 4:6; 6:1, 22. It came from Babylon.

decisions.choice: you: Jerusalem pictured as a woman, responsible for the flock
decisions.reason: The city is spoken of as a woman who was given the towns and people of Judah to care for, like a shepherd's flock. Now she must answer for where they have gone (compare 23:1-2).

decisions.choice: the enemy; the people who were put in your care
decisions.reason: Readable says who is coming and what the flock stands for.

records.source: מַה־תֹּֽאמְרִי֙ כִּֽי־יִפְקֹ֣ד עָלַ֔יִךְ וְ֠אַתְּ לִמַּ֨דְתְּ אֹתָ֥ם עָלַ֛יִךְ אַלֻּפִ֖ים לְרֹ֑אשׁ הֲל֤וֹא חֲבָלִים֙ יֹאחֱז֔וּךְ כְּמ֖וֹ אֵ֥שֶׁת לֵדָֽה׃
records.gloss: What will you say when he appoints over you, and you yourself taught them over you, close friends as head? Will not pangs seize you like a woman of giving birth?
pieces: What will you say when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sets over you as rulers \q the very ones you trained to be your close allies? \q Will not pains grip you \q like a woman in labor?

L.21: What will you say when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} appoints over you as head \q those whom you yourself taught [to be] close friends to you? \q Will not pangs seize you \q like a woman giving birth?

R.21: What will you say when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} puts in charge over you \q the very ones you tried to make your friends? \q You will be in pain \q like a woman giving birth.

decisions.choice: he appoints: the LORD sets them over Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. It is most naturally God, who brings the judgment through the nations; it may instead be the enemy king who sets his officers over the city.

decisions.choice: close friends: allies Jerusalem courted, who now become its masters
decisions.reason: The word can mean an intimate friend (3:4; Proverbs 16:28) or a chief (Genesis 36:15). Both fit: the powers Judah taught to be its friends, by seeking their help (2:18, 36; 2 Kings 20:12-19), become its rulers. The line is hard, and the words may be divided differently.

decisions.choice: pangs like a woman giving birth: sudden, helpless anguish
decisions.reason: The same picture is used of Jerusalem under attack in 4:31; 6:24; 22:23.

decisions.choice: You will be in pain
decisions.reason: Readable gives the question as the statement it implies.

records.source: וְכִ֤י תֹאמְרִי֙ בִּלְבָבֵ֔ךְ מַדּ֖וּעַ קְרָאֻ֣נִי אֵ֑לֶּה בְּרֹ֧ב עֲוֺנֵ֛ךְ נִגְל֥וּ שׁוּלַ֖יִךְ נֶחְמְס֥וּ עֲקֵבָֽיִךְ׃
records.gloss: And if you say in your heart: why have they happened to me, these [things]? In [the] greatness of your iniquity have been uncovered your skirts, have suffered violence your heels.
pieces: And if you ask yourself, \q "Why have these things happened to me?" \q It is because of your great guilt that your skirts have been lifted and your body treated with violence.

L.22: And if you say in your heart, \q "Why have these things come upon me?" \q For the greatness of your iniquity your skirts have been uncovered, your heels have suffered violence.

R.22: You may ask yourself, \q "Why has this happened to me?" \q It is because you have sinned so much. That is why your skirts have been pulled up and you have been cruelly abused.

decisions.choice: skirts uncovered, heels treated with violence: public shaming and abuse
decisions.reason: "Heels" is a polite way of speaking of the private parts, as "feet" sometimes is (Isaiah 7:20). The picture is of a woman stripped and mistreated, as captive women were when a city fell (Isaiah 47:2-3; Nahum 3:5). It is the shame that Jerusalem's sin brings on her.

decisions.choice: treated with violence: wronged, abused
decisions.reason: The verb is related to the common word for violence and wrong (22:3); here it describes rough, shameful handling.

decisions.choice: because of your great iniquity: the disaster is the result of sin
decisions.reason: The question "Why?" is answered: what happens to Jerusalem is not chance but the fruit of her guilt.

decisions.choice: lifted, body treated with violence (Balanced); pulled up, cruelly abused (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable keep the picture in plain, sober words, as at Isaiah 47:2-3, and say "body" or "you" for the polite word "heels".

decisions.choice: guilt (Balanced); sinned (Readable)
decisions.reason: The book's usual wording for this word: "iniquity" at Literal, "guilt" or "sin" at the other levels.

records.source: הֲיַהֲפֹ֤ךְ כּוּשִׁי֙ עוֹר֔וֹ וְנָמֵ֖ר חֲבַרְבֻּרֹתָ֑יו גַּם־אַתֶּם֙ תּוּכְל֣וּ לְהֵיטִ֔יב לִמֻּדֵ֖י הָרֵֽעַ׃
records.gloss: Can change a Cushite his skin, or a leopard its spots? Also you will be able to do good, taught [ones] to do evil.
pieces: Can a Cushite change his skin, \q or a leopard its spots? \q Then you too could do good, \q you who have been schooled in evil.

L.23: Can a Cushite change his skin, \q or a leopard its spots? \q [Then] you also will be able to do good, \q [you who are] taught to do evil.

R.23: Can a person from Cush change the color of his skin? \q Can a leopard change its spots? \q If they could, then you could do good, \q you who are so used to doing evil.

decisions.choice: Cushite: a man from Cush, the land south of Egypt on the upper Nile
decisions.reason: Cush lay in what is now Sudan, and its people were known for their dark skin. Jeremiah's own rescuer, Ebed-melech, was a Cushite (38:7). The point of the saying is only that a thing given by birth cannot be changed, as a leopard cannot remove its spots; it passes no judgment on skin.

decisions.choice: taught: trained, so used to something that it is second nature
decisions.reason: The word echoes "you yourself taught" in verse 21, and describes a wild donkey "used to the wilderness" in 2:24. Evil has become Judah's habit.

decisions.choice: you will be able to do good: you cannot change yourselves
decisions.reason: The question expects the answer no. Sin is so rooted in the people that they cannot turn themselves (17:1, 9); only God can give a new heart (24:7; 31:33).

decisions.choice: the color of; If they could
decisions.reason: Readable says what is meant by changing his skin, and spells out the link between the questions and the answer.

decisions.choice: Cushite
decisions.reason: The Hebrew name of the people is kept, since "Ethiopian", the name in older renderings, now names a different country.

records.source: וַאֲפִיצֵ֖ם כְּקַשׁ־עוֹבֵ֑ר לְר֖וּחַ מִדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And I will scatter them like chaff passing on [the] wind of [the] wilderness.
pieces: I will scatter them like chaff \q blown off by the desert wind.

L.24: And I will scatter them like chaff \q passing on the wind of the wilderness.

R.24: I will scatter them like straw \q that the desert wind blows away.

decisions.choice: chaff on the desert wind: light dry stalks swept away
decisions.reason: The word means stubble or straw left after harvest. The wind from the desert is the hot east wind (4:11; 18:17). The people will be blown to many lands.

decisions.choice: them: the people of Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The poem moves between speaking to the city as "you" (a woman) and of its people as "them".

decisions.choice: chaff (Literal and Balanced); straw (Readable)
decisions.reason: The word is "stubble". "Chaff" is the usual picture of what the wind carries off; Readable uses the plain word "straw".

records.source: זֶ֣ה גוֹרָלֵ֧ךְ מְנָת־מִדַּ֛יִךְ מֵֽאִתִּ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֑ה אֲשֶׁר֙ שָׁכַ֣חַתְּ אוֹתִ֔י וַֽתִּבְטְחִ֖י בַּשָּֽׁקֶר׃
records.gloss: This [is] your lot, [the] portion of your measures from me, declares Yahweh, because you have forgotten me and trusted in falsehood.
pieces: This is your lot, the share I have measured out to you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q because you have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} \q and put your trust in lies.

L.25: This [is] your lot, the portion of your measure from {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q because you have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} \q and trusted in falsehood.

R.25: This is what will happen to you. It is the share I have measured out for you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q You have forgotten {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} \q and trusted in lies.

decisions.choice: lot, portion measured out: the share God assigns
decisions.reason: The words are used for land allotted by lot and measured out to each family (Joshua 18:10; Psalm 16:5-6). Jerusalem's "share" now is judgment.

decisions.choice: falsehood: false gods and false promises
decisions.reason: Jeremiah uses this word for idols (10:14; 16:19) and for the false assurance that the temple would keep them safe (7:4, 8). Both are meant.

decisions.choice: you have forgotten me: broken the covenant
decisions.reason: To forget God is to stop living by his covenant (2:32; 3:21; Deuteronomy 8:11-19).

decisions.choice: This is what will happen to you
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly what "your lot" means.

records.source: וְגַם־אֲנִ֛י חָשַׂ֥פְתִּי שׁוּלַ֖יִךְ עַל־פָּנָ֑יִךְ וְנִרְאָ֖ה קְלוֹנֵֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And also I, I will strip off your skirts over your face, and will be seen your shame.
pieces: So I myself will pull your skirts up over your face, \q and your shame will be there for all to see.

L.26: And I too will strip up your skirts over your face, \q and your shame will be seen.

R.26: I will pull your skirts up over your face, \q and everyone will see your shame.

decisions.choice: I too: God does what her sin has already brought
decisions.reason: The emphatic "I" answers verse 22: the shame she has brought on herself, God now carries out as judge.

decisions.choice: skirts over your face: the public shaming of an unfaithful wife and of a conquered city
decisions.reason: Nahum 3:5 uses the same picture of Nineveh, and Hosea 2:12 and Ezekiel 16:37 of unfaithful Israel and Jerusalem. The covenant faithlessness of verse 27 is answered with public disgrace.

decisions.choice: there for all to see (Balanced); everyone will see (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in Isaiah 47:3, the wording stays plain and sober.

records.gloss: Your adulteries and your neighings, [the] lewdness of your prostitution, on hills in the field I have seen your detestable things. Woe to you, Jerusalem! Not you will be clean; after when yet?
pieces: Your adulteries and your lustful neighing, \q your shameless prostitution on the hills, out in the open country: I have seen your detestable things. \q Woe to you, Jerusalem! \q You will not become clean. How much longer will it be?

L.27: Your adulteries and your neighings, the lewdness of your prostitution \q on the hills in the field, I have seen your detestable things. \q Woe to you, Jerusalem! \q You will not be clean; after how long yet?

R.27: I have seen the disgusting things you have done: \q your adulteries, your lustful cries like a horse's neighing, your shameless prostitution on the hills and in the fields. \q How terrible it will be for you, Jerusalem! \q You will not become clean. How long will this go on?

decisions.choice: adulteries, prostitution: worship of other gods pictured as unfaithfulness in marriage
decisions.reason: Jeremiah, like Hosea, speaks of the covenant as a marriage and of Israel's worship of other gods as adultery (3:1-9; Hosea 2). The hills were the places of the hilltop shrines (2:20; 3:2, 23).

decisions.choice: neighings: unrestrained lust
decisions.reason: Jeremiah compares the people to well-fed stallions neighing after their neighbors' wives (5:8; compare 2:24).

decisions.choice: lewdness; detestable things
decisions.reason: The first word means a deliberate, shameful wickedness, often of sexual sin (Leviticus 18:17). The second is a common word for idols and the rites of other gods (4:1; 7:30).

decisions.choice: you will not be clean; how long yet?: a cry of grief at her lasting uncleanness
alternatives: Will you not be made clean? How long yet?
decisions.reason: The first clause states that Jerusalem stays unclean; the second asks how long that will go on. It may also be read as one question: "Will you not be clean? How long yet?"

decisions.choice: How terrible it will be for you
decisions.reason: The book's usual Readable wording for "woe to".

decisions.choice: I have seen ... placed first
decisions.reason: Readable puts the verb first and lists what God has seen after it, so the long list stays clear.
